paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The Christian life has a real struggle in it, and Paul says it's not against flesh and blood. It's against the spiritual forces of evil (Ephesians 6:12). So Paul doesn't tell you to be tough on your own. He says, "be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power" (Ephesians 6:10).

Now the armor. Paul says to put on the FULL armor of God, and he names the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, the readiness of the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God (Ephesians 6:14-17). Notice what it's all for: to stand. I think that's good news for you, baker, because you don't have to win it all in your own strength. You show up dressed in what God gave you, and you hold your ground.

Then Paul adds prayer, and he doesn't make it a last resort. He says to pray in the Spirit "at all times" and to keep praying for all the saints (Ephesians 6:18). Even Paul, an ambassador in chains, asks the believers to pray for him (Ephesians 6:19-20). So here's your takeaway: get dressed in what God gave you, and keep praying for the people beside you, because nobody stands alone.
